name: SQL-first repository N+1 discipline
short_definition: Keep database access behind thin repository/query modules that express intentional SQLAlchemy 2 `select()` (or Core/text SQL), eager-load or join what the use-case needs, and never rely on async lazy loads. Domain services call repositories with explicit shapes — not open-ended ORM graphs that trigger N+1 or MissingGreenlet.
scope_in: Repository/DAO boundaries; SQLAlchemy 2 style select/where/options; N+1 prevention (selectinload, joinedload, contains_eager, explicit joins); async session lifecycle; read models vs write models; Core/text for hot paths; pagination; transaction boundaries at service layer; mapping DB errors to domain.
scope_out: Migration ownership (py-migrations); pool sizing (py-db-pool-lifecycle); full Supabase client API surface (py-supabase-python); GraphQL dataloaders; search engines; caching strategy details (py-rate-limit-cache).
defaults: SQL-first mental model: every list/get path is a deliberate query module method returning domain DTOs or carefully scoped ORM entities. Prefer `select(Model).where(...).options(...)` with loader options chosen per call site. Async: default relationship lazy strategy should not implicit-IO (`lazy='raise'` or explicit loaders only) — avoid classic lazy='select' on async. Collections: `selectinload` for 1:N/M:N; many-to-one: `joinedload` or join. Use `session.execute` / `scalars` 2.0 API — not legacy Query. Transactions: begin in service/unit-of-work, repositories stay query-focused. For complex reporting or hot paths, Core `select` or `text()` with bound params. Paginate with keyset (preferred) or limit/offset consciously. Never return live Session-bound graphs across HTTP boundaries without rehydration plan.
decision_gates: USE repository methods when: multi-table reads/writes, reuse across routes/workers, need test seams. USE inline select in tiny single-route apps only until second caller appears. USE selectinload when: collections for N parents (avoid cartesian explosion). USE joinedload when: many-to-one / small singular relations. USE Core/SQL when: bulk updates, complex aggregates, planner control. DO NOT lazy-load in async after session closed. DO NOT pass Session into domain pure functions. Hand off to Rust when: extreme query volume / custom engines — still same SQL-first contract.
do_dont: DO: name methods by use-case (`list_open_jobs_for_user`); options() at query site; raiseload('*') in tests to catch accidental loads; map IntegrityError to conflict; close/expire sessions per request. DON'T: for item in items: item.relation (N+1); relationship(lazy='select') with async access; load entire graph 'just in case'; SELECT *; unparameterized text(); commit inside deep repository if service owns unit of work inconsistently; expose ORM models as public API response without serialization boundary.
code_skeleton:
from sqlalchemy import select, func
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload, joinedload, raiseload
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

class JobRepo:
    def __init__(self, session: AsyncSession) -> None:
        self._s = session

    async def get_with_owner(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None:
        stmt = (
            select(Job)
            .where(Job.id == job_id)
            .options(
                joinedload(Job.owner),
                selectinload(Job.events),
                raiseload('*'),  # fail loud on unexpected attrs in strict mode
            )
        )
        return (await self._s.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()

    async def list_for_user(self, user_id: str, *, limit: int = 50) -> list[Job]:
        stmt = (
            select(Job)
            .where(Job.user_id == user_id)
            .order_by(Job.created_at.desc())
            .limit(limit)
            .options(selectinload(Job.tags))
        )
        return list((await self._s.execute(stmt)).scalars().unique().all())

    async def count_open(self, user_id: str) -> int:
        stmt = select(func.count()).select_from(Job).where(
            Job.user_id == user_id, Job.status == 'open'
        )
        return int((await self._s.execute(stmt)).scalar_one())

# Service UoW
async def archive_job(session: AsyncSession, job_id: str) -> None:
    repo = JobRepo(session)
    job = await repo.get_with_owner(job_id)
    if job is None:
        raise NotFoundError('job', job_id)
    job.status = 'archived'
    await session.commit()
failure_modes: 1) N+1 under load from lazy access. 2) MissingGreenlet / greenlet_spawn on async lazy load. 3) Cartesian product from multi-collection joinedload. 4) DetachedInstanceError after session close. 5) Over-fetching huge graphs into memory. 6) OFFSET deep pagination meltdown. 7) Race without proper transaction isolation. 8) Identity map surprises across concurrent tasks sharing session. 9) Silent truncation of results without unique(). 10) Domain logic leaking SQLAlchemy types into OpenAPI models carelessly.
anti_patterns: ActiveRecord god models with business logic + queries everywhere; `session.query` legacy API in new code; lazy='dynamic' as default; loading all rows then filtering in Python; string-interpolated SQL; repositories that return open queries for callers to refine without bounds; one RepositoryBase with 50 generic methods that hide query cost; using sync session in async routes.
tools: SQLAlchemy 2.0 ORM + Core; asyncpg driver; optional sqlparse/SQL explain in staging; pytest + factory fixtures; pytest-asyncio; logging SQL with echo sparingly. Alternatives: raw asyncpg only (max control, more boilerplate); encode/databases (lighter, less ORM); Supabase PostgREST for simple CRUD (boundary, not repository).
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13: SQLAlchemy 2.0.x (2.0 style select is mandatory for greenfield; 1.x Query API legacy). AsyncSession + asyncpg standard. Loader option APIs per SQLAlchemy relationship loading docs (selectinload preferred for collections).

deprecation_watch: SQLAlchemy 1.x `session.query(Model)`; implicit lazy load patterns from Flask-SQLAlchemy tutorials; `subqueryload` as default (prefer selectinload); `joinedload` of multiple large collections together; asyncio.sync_sessionmaker misuse; putting business rules only in DB triggers without app visibility (triggers ok for updated_at, not core domain).
ts_boundary: Next BFF should not reimplement the same multi-join queries when Python owns the write model — call the Python API or use Supabase RLS-scoped simple reads. Share field names via OpenAPI/generated types. Avoid dual-write of the same aggregates from TS and Python.
rust_boundary: Move to Rust/sqlx when a query path is proven CPU/latency critical and stable. Keep SQL text or query ownership clear — do not split one transaction across languages. Prefer one service owns writes for a table set.
supabase_boundary: Direct SQLAlchemy against Postgres is fine for server-side with service role / DB URL — must still respect multi-tenant filters in SQL (do not assume RLS when using service_role). Prefer repository methods that always include tenant/user predicates. PostgREST is alternative for simple CRUD from TS, not a substitute for complex Python write transactions.
boundary_contracts: Repository returns domain DTOs or documented ORM entities; OpenAPI schemas separate from tables; migrations define columns; env DATABASE_URL; no ad-hoc SQL in MCP tools against prod without audit. Transaction boundary documented per use-case (single request vs outbox).
decision_matrix_row: Problem: multi-entity read in Python API → repository + selectinload/joinedload. Problem: simple row CRUD under RLS from browser → Supabase client/TS. Problem: ultra-hot analytical SQL → Core/text or Rust. Problem: graph over-fetch → explicit read model query, not full ORM tree.
threats: IDOR if repository omits authz filters under service_role; SQL injection via f-strings; mass assignment through ORM; data exfil via unbounded queries; timing via error differences on not-found.
mitigations: Always parameterize; enforce tenant predicates in repo; limit/limit max page size; never trust client-side field filters alone; use RLS when using user-scoped DB roles; map errors without leaking existence where required; least privilege DB roles for app.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST: SQLAlchemy 2 select API; eager options or raiseload for async; use-case-named repo methods; bound parameters; pagination caps. MUST NOT: N+1 loops; lazy load after await without loader; session.query; SELECT without WHERE on multi-tenant tables; interpolate user input into SQL text.
tests_required: Unit: repo methods with test DB/testcontainers; assert query count (N+1 guards); integrity conflict mapping; pagination limits. Integration: FastAPI path with real session. Optional: explain analyze snapshots for hot queries.
ci_gates: pytest with async DB tests; banlist grep for session.query( and for rel in .*:\n.*for ; basedpyright on repo modules; optional SQLAlchemy warn on lazy.
skill_scan_signals: POSITIVE: select(, selectinload, joinedload, AsyncSession, use-case repo methods, raiseload, keyset/limit pagination. NEGATIVE: session.query, for x in items: x.relation without options, lazy='select' + async access, f"SELECT ... {user}", unbounded .all() on large tables, ORM models returned raw without schema boundary.
skill_module_bullets:
- SQL-first repositories: intentional select() per use-case.
- Async: no implicit lazy loads — selectinload/joinedload/raiseload.
- selectinload for collections; joinedload for many-to-one.
- Service owns transactions; repo owns queries.
- Cap pagination; parameterize all SQL.
- service_role paths must still filter tenant/user in SQL.
- Prefer DTOs at API boundary over open ORM graphs.

[ ] Loader options on every multi-relation read
[ ] No async lazy loads

conflicts_noted: ActiveRecord vs repository debates: for services with workers + API, thin repositories win for testability. selectinload vs joinedload: docs prefer selectinload for collections; some prefer joinedload for single many-to-one — both valid. Pure SQL vs ORM purity: hybrid is correct (ORM for CRUD graphs, Core for hot/bulk). Unit-of-work commit in repo vs service — pick one team rule; this research prefers service-level commit.
